items.title: Real money flows on open-autonomy.org
acceptance: Owner-gated (identity and a bank, not code): a Polar organization for Open Autonomy and the org's Stripe account with Issuing, their tokens and webhook secrets installed through the admin workflow's secret sync, the webhook endpoints enrolled; everything else is already proven against the twins.

One real patronage lands on this project's books through Polar, its payout reaches the org, the Issuing balance is funded from it, and this install's agent makes one real bounded purchase that shows on the audit trail.

items.title: The kit's template is used the way it is written
acceptance: In the world, with the todo-cli cookbook, every part of the template is exercised and read back through the product's doors: the developer files a purchase and blocks with needs_input, the treasurer profile pays it on its own key and releases it with a receipt, the review lane checks the handoff against CONSTITUTION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md and its verdict names them, the PM's hour unsticks a transient block and leaves a needs_input block and a parked task alone, the reporter publishes the board, the sessions and the two documents to the page.
Anything the template says that the world shows is not happening is fixed in the template, never papered over in the cookbook.

items.title: A second cookbook with a community gateway: Discord, GitHub issues and discussions, a GitHub Pages homepage
acceptance: A cookbook whose agent takes work and questions from its community as well as its board: a Discord channel, the repository's issues and discussions; triage files board tasks, answers land where they were asked, and every conversation the agent has in public is a published session.
Its homepage is a GitHub Pages site the agent maintains from the repository, carrying the project's page widgets.
Proven only in the world, against twins of Discord and of GitHub's issues and discussions (the GitHub twin extended where it must be), with nothing in the cookbook calling a real API.

items.title: notes-api runs in the world since the bare cut
acceptance: `WORLD_STATE_ROOT=/Users/yueranyuan/.local/state/open-autonomy/open-autonomy/home/world bun world/run.ts up --cookbook notes-api` brings the world up in your container and the notes-api board works its seed tasks to done: every task lands as a merged pull request on the GitHub twin, and the sessions show on the world's project page with their item ids and cost (world/README.md is how to drive it; `bun world/run.ts hermes kanban list` is the board).
Whatever stops it is fixed where it lives: world/handlers/notes-api (its scenario and stages) or cookbooks/notes-api, never by skipping a task.
`bun run check` green; `down --purge` when done.

items.title: Spend lands on the session that made the call, even when sessions overlap
acceptance: Today the ledger attributes a settled model call to the one live session of the account and leaves it unattributed when several are live (apps/platform/src/ledger.ts, attributeSpend). A worker, its reviewer and the PM overlap as a matter of course, so most sessions show 0 calls and 0 cents on the page while the books are right. Every call must land on the session that made it: find the door by which a call can name its session between Hermes, the valve (packages/sdk/src/valve.ts, vendored as .open-autonomy/sdk/valve.ts) and the platform's proxy, and use it; guessing from liveness goes away.

Verified in your world: with the todo-cli cookbook the worker, the reviewer and the PM run at once (`hermes cron run pm` while a worker runs); on the world's project page every ended session shows its own calls and cents, the item page sums them, and the account's consumed_usd_cents equals the sum over sessions plus nothing unattributed.

The books stay authoritative: consumed_usd_cents is never derived from sessions. CONSTITUTION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md hold; the kit's template changes go with a kit version bump and the cookbooks upgraded (bun packages/kit-hermes/src/cli.ts upgrade <dir>).
If the only door is a change in Hermes itself, block with exactly what Hermes lacks and where.

items.title: The project page shows what its funds may buy and how fast, and says when a session ran on a subscription
acceptance: The account's JSON already carries `bounds` (the allowed models, and each spend limit with its window and its use: apps/platform/src/ledger.ts). The project page (apps/platform/src/site.ts and stream-view.tsx) shows them where the budget is shown: the models the funds may buy, and every limit as used-of-bound over its window, in the page's own idiom (the runway and daily spend are the neighbours). No new endpoint: read what the JSON already says.

A session whose model calls never touched the platform (its agent runs on the owner's subscription, so it has no calls and no cents) says so on the page instead of showing 0 ¢: the reporter already knows the session's provider; carry what is needed through the SDK's session events without publishing anything that is a secret, and let the page render it. Whatever is not known stays absent, never guessed.

Verified in your world with the todo-cli cookbook: its page shows the three default limits with use rising as the board works; and in a world run whose agent config names a custom provider that is not the platform (a bare `custom_providers` entry with a fake base URL is enough to prove the label; the calls may fail), the session shows the subscription label. CONSTITUTION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md hold; a template change means a kit version bump and the cookbooks upgraded.

items.title: The page renders a project's documents as markdown, not as raw text
acceptance: On the project page (apps/platform/src/site.tsx and stream-view.tsx), the sections published from a project's documents — What's shipped (CHANGELOG.md) and About (CONSTITUTION.md, and its full page) — render inline markdown: bold, code spans, links, and nested lists, the way the session and task text already renders. Today a visitor sees literal `**` and backticks in What's shipped on every project page (open-autonomy.org/p/open-autonomy-org%2Fhookline shows it).
The renderer is the one the page already has for markdown elsewhere, or a small one beside it; no dependency added; untrusted input stays escaped (a document is repository content, never HTML).

Verified in your world: the todo-cli cookbook's page shows its CHANGELOG entries with bold and code rendered, and its About page renders headings, lists and links. CONSTITUTION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md hold.

items.title: A funder gives from a page: sign in with GitHub, see your credits, pick a project, give — and the owner passes Sponsors money on the same way
acceptance: `GET /give` is a page. Signed out, it explains grant credits and offers "Sign in with GitHub"; the sign-in is GitHub's OAuth for a registered app (client id and secret as Worker secrets), asks for no scope beyond the login, and results in a signed, expiring session cookie that stands for the funder `@login` — it can only give, exactly as a funder key can.

Signed in, the page shows the funder's credits and every gift they have made, a project picker over the platform's projects, an amount, and the earmark control; giving is one submit and lands on the project's books with the funder's name, idempotent on a key the page mints per attempt.

An org admin signed in sees the org's grants pool as a second source they may give from, so Sponsors money is passed on from this page and not from a workflow; who passed what on is on the pool's flow history.
The key-based path (`/v1/keys/challenge`, `/v1/keys/mint`, `/v1/grants/give`) stays as it is; the page is a second door onto the same books.

Security bar: the cookie is HMAC-signed with a dedicated secret, bound to the login and an expiry, never to a key; a forged or expired cookie is refused; the OAuth state is checked; nothing in the page can spend or steer.

Proven in the world against the GitHub twin's OAuth: a funder signs in, gives with an earmark, the project's page shows the gift and the envelope; a second give with the same idempotency key is not doubled.

items.title: A patron knows what happens at zero and how to stop: one sentence each beside the tiers
acceptance: Beside the tiers, one sentence says what happens when the balance reaches zero: the agent stops, nothing is lost, the balance and every receipt stay on the page, and the next gift starts it again.

One sentence says how a patron ends or changes a recurring gift: through GitHub Sponsors' own page for a GitHub sponsorship, through Polar's customer portal for a Polar one — the platform never holds a card and cannot cancel for them.
The sentences live in the page's own words (site.tsx), not in a linked document, and read the same on every project page.
Proven in the world: the todo-cli project page shows both sentences in the funding block.

items.title: A gift can say what it is for: earmarks on the books, drawn first when a spend qualifies, released when the purpose is met
acceptance: An account's funds are envelopes: unrestricted, or restricted to one of exactly four purposes — any spend; the model rail only; the model rail on a named list of models; one roadmap item by id. A grant (`POST /v1/grants/give`) and a Polar checkout carry an optional `for` naming one; absent means unrestricted. Money already on the books is untouched.

A reserve draws from the most specific qualifying envelope first, then the less specific, then unrestricted; the consumed call record names the envelope it drew from. A spend that no remaining envelope qualifies for is refused with `insufficient_funds` and a message naming what the remaining money is earmarked for and how much; the agent's provider sees that message.

An earmark for an item is refused at give time (`no_such_item`) when the item is not on the project's roadmap. When an earmarked item reaches done, its remaining balance is released to unrestricted and the account's flow history records the release with the item and the amount.
The owner's bounds (`models:`, `spend.limits`) still apply on top: an earmark narrows, never widens.
The account JSON lists the envelopes (purpose, balance, from whom) and the runway estimate counts only money the project's next spend could use.

Proven in the world: a grant earmarked to an item is drawn by a session serving that item and refused to one that is not, with the refusal's words; an earmark to a model list is drawn only by calls on those models; finishing the item releases the rest and the flow history shows it.

items.title: The page shows funds as envelopes, and every receipt says which one paid
acceptance: The funding block lists the unrestricted balance and each envelope beneath it as one line: amount, purpose in plain words ("the task 'The inbox is the owner's to read'", "model calls on zai/glm-5.3-flash"), and who gave it, linking to the gift.
A session's calls and the item page's receipts name the envelope each call drew from; a release appears in the funding history as "task done; $X released to whatever <project> needs".

The tier picker carries the giver's choice as one control with three options — whatever the project needs (default), model calls only, a task chosen from the roadmap's open items — and the Polar checkout and thanks page repeat the choice back in one sentence, including the release rule.
The days-funded line counts only money the next spend could use, and says so when earmarked money is excluded.

Proven in the world: the todo-cli page with two earmarked gifts and one unrestricted shows three lines, a call receipt names its envelope, and a checkout made with the task option comes back to a thanks page that names the task.

items.title: The page says what is live against what has landed, from the commit the service reports
acceptance: A project whose `.open-autonomy/config.yaml` names `live: <url>` (the address of its deployed service; Hookline's answers `GET /api` with `{name, version}`, the platform's own answers its health check with the commit) is read by the platform on the same schedule as its config: the live commit (a short SHA) and the default branch's head from the repository's own API.

The account JSON carries `live: {commit, head, ahead}` — `ahead` the count of commits on the default branch since the live commit (GitHub's compare endpoint), null when the live commit is unknown or not an ancestor — and the project page shows one line in the header: "live: <sha> · main is N changes ahead" linking the compare, or "live: <sha> · up to date", or nothing when the project names no live address.
A service that does not answer, or answers without a commit, shows "live: unreachable" rather than a stale number; nothing is cached across a failed read.

Proven in the world: the todo-cli project with a `live:` address pointed at a world service that reports a commit shows the line, the count moves when a commit lands, and an unreachable address shows as such.

items.title: The project reaches out when a human must act: a hook on the board's blocked lane, the owner told through the project's door, the PM asking again until it is done
acceptance: `hermes/hooks/escalate/` (kit-owned, beside the seed hook) runs on `on_kanban_task_updated`: when a task enters `blocked` with kind `needs_input` or `capability`, it subscribes the owner to that task with `hermes kanban notify-subscribe <task> --delivery-mode notify+wake` on the project's chat door (the platform and chat id from `hermes/config.yaml`'s `owner:` block: `owner: {discord: <user id>}`), so the board messages the owner and wakes the agent to say, in its own voice, what it needs and the exact command or click that unblocks it. When the task leaves blocked, the subscription is removed.

A project with no chat door escalates through its GitHub App instead: the hook opens one issue per blocked task titled from the task, body the block reason and the unblocking step, assigned to the owner (`owner: {github: <login>}`); it closes the issue when the task is unblocked. `.open-autonomy/community.ts` grows `issue open|close` for this, through the valve's door like the rest.

The develop skill: a block for a human states the ask as an action the owner can take — the command, the page, the secret's name — never only the symptom; the worker names the kind (`needs_input` for a fact or a secret, `capability` for a permission it cannot get).

The PM skill: every hour, every task still blocked for a human is asked again through the same door in one message; a project whose live address is behind main (the platform's `live.ahead` on the account JSON) gets a standing task "ship what has landed" blocked `needs_input` with the tag command (`git tag -a deploy-v<date> <head> && git push origin <tag>`) as the ask, unblocked by the PM itself when `ahead` returns to zero. The PM never cuts a tag, never deploys.
The setup writes `owner:` from the signed-in login and the chosen doors; `hermes/config.yaml` stays the project's own.

Proven in the world: a worker blocks a task `needs_input` in the todo-cli world; the Discord twin shows the owner messaged and the agent's own message naming the unblocking command; the same in the GitHub twin as an issue when the world has no chat door; the PM's next pass asks again; unblocking closes the issue and ends the subscription.

items.title: A project takes the kit's upgrades itself: the PM sees a newer kit, lands the upgrade, and the gateway comes forward on its own
acceptance: The PM skill, each hour: compare `.open-autonomy/kit.json`'s version with `npm view create-open-autonomy version`; when npm is newer, run `bunx create-open-autonomy@<v> upgrade .` on a `land/kit-<v>` branch off a fresh origin/main, commit, push; the landing merges it. The PM never edits a kit-owned file by hand and never upgrades when a task is running (it waits for the next idle hour).

The start script notices a landed upgrade: when the checkout's `.open-autonomy/kit.json` version differs from the one the running gateway started with (recorded in the home at start), the PM's report says so and the gateway's own supervisor restarts it at the next idle moment — `hermes gateway restart` from the PM's shell when no task is running, which brings the checkout to origin/main and re-syncs the home the way every start does.

A kit upgrade that touches `.github/` waits for the owner like any workflow change; the PM's report names the pull request and asks through the project's door (the reach-out task's mechanism) rather than waiting silently.

Proven in the world: the todo-cli world with a newer kit on the npm registry twin: the PM lands the upgrade, the page's setup shows the new kit version after the restart, and no task in flight was interrupted.

items.title: A week untouched: the projects run seven days with no human act but a tag and its approval
acceptance: Owner-gated, and not code: after the reach-out hook, self-upgrade and live-versus-landed are live, Hookline and this project run seven consecutive days in which the only human acts are cutting a tag and approving its run. Every blocked task in that week reached its owner through the project's own door; every kit release was taken by the project's PM; every landed change was asked for, not noticed.
What ends it early is a task for the kit, filed by the owner, and the week starts over.
The evidence is the pages: seven days of sessions, the board's history, the release and deploy runs, and no maintainer commit but tags.

items.title: Prepare and verify the 2.8.2 onboarding artifact
acceptance: Advance create-open-autonomy to 2.8.2 and upgrade this repository and all cookbooks normally without changing the landed setup behavior.

Run the canonical root check, inspect the 2.8.2 and SDK 2.4.1 package tarballs, and exercise installation plus protected-branch claim/owner-policy paths in the world as far as the GitHub twin supports them.
Report Docker ownership, delayed-review auto-merge, live GitHub authorization and executable-runtime provenance limits explicitly; do not claim production evidence.
Hand off for review; do not publish, tag or deploy.

acceptance: bun run check and bun scripts/check-supply-chain.ts pass for the selected candidate, and the package tarballs contain the intended 2.10.0, 3.0.0 and backend 0.3.0 artifacts.
The review package names the exact candidate, versions, scope, risks and authorized tag commands.
A maintainer must still review the exact candidate and explicitly approve both human-cut tags and their production-environment runs.
The service deployment is verified separately from npm publication; neither is inferred from the other.
The live /healthz response still does not name a commit, so production status for the latest deploy tag is not independently verifiable yet.
The installed GitHub App exposes PR, review, workflow, tag and release evidence; no replacement candidate, maintainer approval, release run or matching release tag exists yet.

Docker UID isolation/token refresh and delayed-review native auto-merge remain unverified end to end after PR #493; candidate preparation must preserve these as explicit operational risks rather than claiming live proof.

Local Codex in the container is unverified: the start script's forwarding through the valve's Codex port has not yet carried one real model turn on a Docker host.

Verified owner yueranyuan closed PR #594 with comment 5648467119, affirming accepted ADR 0001 as the replacement for that superseded runtime proposal. This resolves the authority conflict recorded from PR #593; the remaining container turn and model-twin observations are verification risks, not scope authority gaps.

Owner-authored PR #611 and ADR 0003 landed at approved head fda82472, bringing unpublished kit 2.9.0, SDK 2.5.0 and backend 0.2.0 manifests to main. The live-run pause window remains unexercised, and no package publication or deployment is implied.

The giving UI requires GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and GIVE_SESSION_HMAC_SECRET; production activation remains a separate held outcome until their approved installation and a live check are evidenced.

items.title: Prepare the replacement onboarding and backend artifacts
acceptance: Preserve PR #551's sharp@0.35.4 remediation and confirm the selected candidate's supply-chain scan remains green without weakening or editing the protected security workflow.

Reconcile reviewed manifests at create-open-autonomy 2.10.0, @open-autonomy/sdk 3.0.0 and @open-autonomy/backend 0.3.0, upgrade this repository and every cookbook normally, and inspect all three package tarballs.
Run the canonical root check, hand off for independent review and report the remaining Docker, delayed-review, live-GitHub and executable-provenance gaps. Do not publish, tag or deploy.

items.title: The bare and containerized fleets look the same; the container forwards
acceptance: Bare: both profiles use native Hermes openai-codex through the host valve and transient access from the installed Codex app-server; no login is copied into project or Hermes storage, a missing current computer login fails closed, and autonomous use has the required OS-user credential boundary.

Container: Hermes receives only a stand-in credential and forwards through the host valve/Codex app-server boundary; the login never enters the executor. Prove one real turn in the managed container on a Docker host.
The project-owned World scenario points the provider at its model twin through HERMES_CODEX_BASE_URL; a native agent turn passes through that endpoint.

items.title: The owner's running or paused word travels through the SDK
acceptance: A steer-scoped owner request records running or paused; an arbitrary automation reads it through the SDK, applies it by its own method and reports the truth through the SDK, while the platform only records and displays desired versus observed state.

The Hermes kit stops scheduled work without interrupting a live run, reports paused only when no job is enabled or running, and resumes exactly the jobs it paused; state survives reload and failures remain visible.

Exercise the live-run pause window through the disposable World product path: while a run is active, a pause request remains visibly desired-paused/observed-running, the run finishes without interruption, then the reporter disables scheduled work and reports paused. Recheck this after the current reporter stack settles. Release, publication and deployment remain separate gates.

items.title: The SDK is the automation interface, not its host machinery
acceptance: Landed in PR #618: reserve paused for the owner's operating state and call a funded balance spent to zero exhausted without changing the ledger's spending behavior.
Carry automation reporting, including the timeline, through the events door; keep roadmap mutation on the owner's steer-only door and return truthful status/error receipts for every client write.

Keep SDK 3.0 to the public automation interface, codecs, drivers, roster and key helpers; relocate host tools to the kit and owner-config parsing to the backend without weakening credential, runtime or publication boundaries.

Remove the platform's Hermes-shaped task/board record: item status is the lane, sessions are attempts, and review verdicts/handoffs arrive exactly once as restart-durable item updates. Exercise that path manually in the World.
Satisfy the ADR process for the material wire/package/platform-responsibility changes and remove all persistent automated test code or test edits from the proposed diff before exact-head approval.

items.title: Activate and verify the signed-in giving page in production
acceptance: A maintainer provisions the GitHub OAuth app and installs GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and GIVE_SESSION_HMAC_SECRET through a reviewed production authority path; no agent receives them.
On the deployed service, a funder signs in, sees credits, makes one idempotent earmarked gift, and the project's public books show the matching envelope.

items.title: Run seven days with no human act but release review and shipping
acceptance: After live-versus-landed status, owner outreach and self-upgrade are live for this project and Hookline, the owner starts the clock.

Both projects then run for seven consecutive days in which the only human acts are cutting an approved tag and approving its run; every human block reaches the owner, every kit release is adopted by PM, and every landed change is requested rather than merely noticed.
A kit defect filed during the observation ends it and starts a new seven-day window after correction. Evidence is the published sessions, board history and release/deploy runs.

items.title: Real money flows on open-autonomy.org
acceptance: The owner establishes a Polar organization and the org's live Stripe account with Issuing, installs the tokens and webhook secrets through the reviewed admin workflow, and enrolls the webhook endpoints.

One real patronage lands on this project's books through Polar, its payout reaches the org, the Issuing balance is funded from it, and this install's agent makes one real bounded purchase recorded on the public audit trail.
